# Key metrics from VCF files

## Depth 

For each file in `bcftools_stats_datafiles/` directory, we will extract the depth of coverage information. The depth of coverage is a measure of how many times a given base in the genome is sequenced. This information can be useful for identifying regions of the genome that are poorly covered or over-covered.

The depth info is extracted using:
```{bash}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false

for file in bcftools_stats_datafiles/*.txt; do
  grep "^PSC" $file
done

```


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
depth_colnames <- c("PSC", "id","sample","nRefHom","nNonRefHom","nHets","nTransitions","nTransversions","nIndels","average_depth","nSingletons","nHapRef","nHapAlt","nMissing")
  
# Raw data (6.2 SNPs)
depth_raw <- read.delim("./bcftools_stats_datafiles/depths_per_sample.raw.tsv", col.names = depth_colnames) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-PSC, -id)
head(depth_raw)
```
Plot the depth distribution
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

# Plot distribution of fraction_sites_percentage
depth_raw %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = sample, y = average_depth)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(group = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Depth per sample",
       x = "IVIP",
       y = "Average depth") +
  theme_minimal()

# plot distribution of read depth 
depth_raw %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = average_depth)) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(title = "Depth distribution") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
